c: Willow Creek Brewing, a craft brewery that wants to build a larger production facility
s: Willow Creek Brewing's sales have grown 30% a year and the taproom is often full. The company needs $1.2 million to expand production and is considering a bank loan or bringing in an investor.

The chief financial officer (judge) wants you to explain the differences between borrowing and selling ownership, what the company should consider before choosing, and how risk should affect the decision.
p: Explain types of financing (debt and equity)
Calculate the cost of credit
Determine factors affecting business risk
Describe the nature of cash flow statements
Explain the role of finance in business
n: Debt requires repayment with interest but keeps ownership; equity shares ownership and profits
Compares interest cost, repayment terms, collateral and control
Considers whether projected cash flow can cover payments in a slow season
Matches the choice to growth plans and tolerance for risk
q: What would happen to the company if sales dropped 25% after the expansion?
Would you recommend a fixed or variable interest rate? Why?

s: A local landscaping company has applied for a $75,000 line of credit to buy equipment. Its sales have been steady, but its profit is thin and a large customer owes it $40,000 that is 90 days late.
The commercial lending manager (judge) wants you to explain how to evaluate the application, what financial information to review, and whether you would recommend approval, conditions or denial.
p: Explain the purposes and importance of credit
Validate credit history
Interpret statistical findings
Determine factors affecting business risk
Discuss considerations in selecting a financial-services provider
n: Reviews the five Cs: character, capacity, capital, collateral and conditions
Examines financial statements, cash flow and credit history
Notes risk of the overdue receivable and customer concentration
Recommends terms such as a smaller limit, collateral or covenants
q: What would make you more comfortable approving the full amount?
How would you explain a denial to a hard-working business owner?

c: Anchor Insurance Partners, a commercial insurance agency
s: A local bakery owner was surprised to learn her policy did not cover income lost during a three-week closure after a kitchen fire. She says nobody explained what the policy included.
The agency principal (judge) wants you to explain the concept of insurance, how businesses decide what coverage they need, and how you would communicate policy limits so clients are not surprised.
p: Describe the concept of insurance
Explain the nature of risk management
Explain legal considerations for finance
Reinforce service orientation through communication
Describe types of financial-services providers
n: Insurance transfers risk from one party to a pool in exchange for a premium
Identifies property, liability, business interruption and employee coverage needs
Names exclusions, deductibles and limits in plain language
Follows up in writing and reviews coverage annually
q: Why might a business choose a higher deductible?
What would you say to a client who wants to skip a coverage to save money?

c: Trident Manufacturing, which sells machinery in North America and Europe
s: Trident Manufacturing invoices some customers in euros. When the euro fell against the dollar last year, the company received less than it expected on several large orders. The treasurer also worries about rising interest rates on the company's variable-rate loan.
The treasurer (judge) wants you to explain how exchange rates and interest rates affect a business, and what steps the company can take to reduce those risks.
p: Explain the economic impact of interest-rate fluctuations
Discuss the global environment in which businesses operate
Explain the nature of global trade
Determine factors affecting business risk
Explain the time value of money
n: Rates change loan costs, customer demand and investment decisions
Currency changes can increase or reduce revenue from foreign sales
Mentions invoicing in dollars, hedging, fixed-rate debt and diversifying markets
Explains why money received later is worth less
q: Would you recommend hedging all of the currency risk? Why or why not?
How would a rate increase change your plans to buy new equipment?

s: Nova Software's finance team spends days each month collecting figures from spreadsheets. Reports sometimes disagree, and executives do not trust the numbers in meetings.
The finance director (judge) wants you to explain how the team can manage financial information more reliably, which technology would help, and how to present results clearly to executives.
p: Explain the role of information systems
Evaluate quality and source of information
Maintain data security
Select and use appropriate graphic aids
Write executive summaries
n: Centralizes data in one system and automates repeat tasks
Checks that data is accurate, current and reconciled
Controls access and keeps audit trails
Uses charts to show trends and variances
Opens with a short summary of what changed and what to do
q: What would you do if two reports showed different revenue totals?
How do you present bad news to executives?
